speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and what it looked like when you first noticed it? Also, do you have any recent history of insect bites, animal scratches, or travel to rural areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Leishmaniasis

I have noted your history of the ant bite one month prior to the lesion's appearance, along with your significant immune-compromising conditions like Crohn's disease and recent steroid use for uveitis. Given the ulcerative nature and chronic progression, I need to confirm the specific type of Leishmaniasis.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Peripheral Blood Smear
REQUEST TEST: Leishmaniasis Serology (ELISA)
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photo of the right leg lesion
